tarifs.pricingFaq1Q: Can I cancel my subscription at any time?
tarifs.pricingFaq1A: Yes, absolutely. You can cancel your subscription at any time from your account settings, with no notice or extra fees. Access remains active until the end of the current billing period.
tarifs.pricingFaq2Q: Does the Pro plan include all DuupFlow modules?
tarifs.pricingFaq2A: Yes. The Pro plan unlocks every module: Image Duplication, Video Duplication, Similarity Comparator and AI Masking. All formats are supported and copies are unlimited.
tarifs.pricingFaq3Q: How many files can I process per month with the Pro plan?
tarifs.pricingFaq3A: There is no limit on the number of files or copies generated. You can import as many files as you want and create as many variants as needed, with no monthly restriction.
tarifs.pricingFaq4Q: Will I be guided to get started?
tarifs.pricingFaq4A: Yes. Human support is available 7 days a week to help you master the tool and use it in the most effective way: recommended settings for your platforms, duplication best practices, reposting strategy. You are never left alone with the tool.
tarifs.pricingFaq5Q: Which plan is right for me?
tarifs.pricingFaq5A: It all depends on your posting cadence. Posting a few pieces of content per week to get started: Starter is more than enough. Publishing daily and recycling your best videos: Solo is the best volume-for-money. Managing several accounts or clients with high volume: Pro, with its unlimited caps, is built for that. And you can switch plans at any time.
tarifs.pricingFaq6A: Billing is monthly and automatic. You receive an invoice by email at each renewal. We accept Visa, Mastercard and American Express through our partner Stripe.
tarifs.pricingFaq7Q: What's the video limit of the AI editor?
tarifs.pricingFaq7A: The AI editor uses your video duplication quota: 300 renders per month on the Solo plan, and unlimited on the Pro plan. Every video Claude edits counts against that quota.
tarifs.pricingFaq8Q: How is AI Variation billing handled?
tarifs.pricingFaq8A: AI Variation is billed pay-per-use via a token system (1 token = €0.40). The price per image depends on your plan: €1.10 on Free, €0.90 on Solo, €0.70 on Pro. You top up whenever you want, no commitment. If a generation fails (NSFW, technical error), your tokens are refunded automatically.

durationInfo.title: Why duration varies
durationInfo.body: The longer and higher-quality your files are, the longer duplications take to generate. This is completely normal: DuupFlow works hard to preserve the original quality of your files.

docs.title: Documentation
docs.filtersTitle: Which filters to choose for your use case
docs.filtersIntro: Each pack changes a different layer of the video, and you can stack them. Here's when to use each one:
docs.filtersMeta: Metadata — date, encoder, brand, identifier. Invisible to the eye: keep it always on, it's the base for making every copy unique.
docs.filtersMetaTech: Technical metadata — bitrate, GOP, FPS, H.264 profile. Varies the file's technical signature without touching the image.
docs.filtersPixel: Magic pixel — imperceptible luma noise for a 100% unique hash. Ideal to repost with no visible change at all.
docs.filtersAudio: Audio — volume, light EQ, bitrate. Turn it on if the soundtrack should differ too.
docs.filtersMotion: Motion — slight zoom and rotation. Subtle visual variation, useful if platforms compare the image.
docs.filtersVisuals: Visuals — hue, sharpness, EQ. Stronger visual variation, when you really want to move away from the original.
docs.filtersReco: To repost discreetly (no visible change): Metadata + Technical metadata + Magic pixel. Add Motion or Visuals if you want a stronger visible difference.
docs.tiktokBody: A complete guide to repost on TikTok without getting flagged:
docs.advancedIntro: Advanced mode doesn't use preset packs: you set every parameter of every duplication, manually and precisely. It's the mode for users who want full control over how each copy turns out.
docs.advancedManual: Manual per-duplication settings — define the exact values (zoom, rotation, speed, colors, metadata…) for each copy, one by one.
docs.advancedPrecise: Precise control — ideal for agencies and high volumes that need very fine, reproducible modifications.
docs.advancedNoAuto: No forced automation — nothing is applied for you, you decide every variation.
docs.advancedTemplates: 💾 Tip: once your settings are perfect, save them as a template to re-apply them in one click next time — handy to keep consistency across your duplications.
docs.advancedSupport: 🙌 Not sure which settings to choose? Contact support (button at the bottom left): we'll help you set the right parameters for your goal.
docs.detNoticeP1: This module removes all AI metadata, including the C2PA manifests used by Meta / Threads.
docs.detNoticeP2: ⚠️ Heads up: some platforms also use visual-content detection (pixels, patterns) that's independent of metadata.
docs.detNoticeTip: To get around that layer, first run your file through the Image Duplication module to apply subtle visual micro-variations.
docs.imgUsageBody: The Images module generates several unique copies of the same image.
docs.imgUsageB1: Different EXIF/XMP metadata on each copy.
docs.imgUsageB2: Visual micro-variations imperceptible to the eye.
docs.imgUsageReco: 🎯 Ideal to repost across several accounts without being seen as a duplicate.
docs.imgOptFund: Fundamentals — randomizes the metadata (EXIF/XMP). Keep it on, it's the base.
docs.imgOptSemi: Semi — imperceptible pixel tweak for a unique hash.
docs.imgOptIphone: iPhone — injects realistic Apple EXIF metadata.
docs.imgOptCountry: Country — adds a GPS location to the metadata.
docs.imgOptionsIntro: DuupFlow groups the options by their visual impact:
docs.cmpUsageBody: The compressor reduces the weight of your images and videos, with no loss visible to the eye.
docs.cmpUsageGuarantee: ✅ Guarantee: the output file is never heavier than the original.
docs.cmpLevelBalanced: Balanced — the best quality / weight trade-off (recommended).
docs.comparatorUsageBody: The comparator measures how similar two files are and derives a single score: image analysis (perceptual fingerprint) counts for 60%, technical metadata (container, tags, bitrates, filename) for 40%. Structural fields — container, codec, stream count — are shown but excluded from the score: two files of the same nature cannot differ on them.
docs.comparatorUsageReco: 🎯 Check that a copy is different enough from the original to stay undetectable.
docs.comparatorScoreHigh: High score — the files look too alike, risk of being seen as a duplicate.
docs.comparatorScoreLow: Low score — well differentiated, the copy is safe to repost.
docs.comparatorGreen: 🟢 Everything shown in green is what differs between the two files.
docs.varUsageBody: AI Variation creates automatic, unique versions of your content using AI.
docs.varUsageReco: ✨ From a single source image, get several versions ready to publish.
docs.varCostReco: 💡 The cost per image depends on your plan (see Plan & tokens).
docs.apiUsageBody: The DuupFlow API lets you automate DuupFlow from your own tools (Make, n8n, Claude Code).
docs.advicePrincipleBody: Platforms don't just read your files' metadata: they COMPARE THE IMAGES themselves. Two copies that look alike on screen are recognised as the same content, even with completely different metadata.
docs.advicePrincipleKey: The direct consequence: the STRONGER the visual difference between your copies, the better it works. Subtle settings aren't enough — you need bold variations.
docs.adviceCase1Title: Case 1 — Your video has no on-screen text
docs.adviceCase1Intro: This is by far the best situation to be in. Two settings to turn on:
docs.adviceCase1Reverse: Reverse (horizontal mirror) — THE most effective one, use it first. Your video looks exactly the same to a viewer, but becomes completely different to an algorithm, since every pixel moves.
docs.adviceCase1Watermark: Watermark — strongly recommended on top. It adds a layer that moves and changes on every copy.
docs.adviceCase1Warning: One thing to watch: the mirror also flips burnt-in text, logos and any writing visible in the scene. If your video has any, go to case 2.
docs.adviceCase2Title: Case 2 — Your video is already edited (mirroring isn't an option)
docs.adviceCase2Intro: On-screen text? An edit already done? Then don't try to disguise the same footage: make REAL new versions of it with the AI Editor.
docs.adviceCase2Step1: Take your original video, the one WITHOUT the edit, and give it as source footage.
docs.adviceCase2Step2: Add your already-edited video as the reference, so the style is preserved.
docs.adviceCase2Step3: Ask Claude for several variants, each with a different edit.
docs.adviceCase2Why: You no longer get retouched copies but genuinely different edits: cuts, pacing and framing all change. That's what looks most like original content.
docs.adviceCase3Intro: That leaves the blunt approach: push the motion filters to the maximum in duplication.
docs.adviceCase3Body: Zoom, rotation, cropping, shake: applied boldly, they move the image enough to widen the gap between your files.
docs.adviceCase3Warning: Know this before you do it: your videos will be visually degraded. That's the price, and it's a deliberate trade-off — more difference between copies, lower quality. Keep it for cases where the mirror and the AI Editor are both out of reach.
docs.motionPacksIntro: Both act on the FRAMING, but not in the same way. Each has a « Gentle / Strong » toggle on its card: same mechanism, two scales. Here's which one to pick and what it does exactly.
docs.motionClassicTitle: Motion — the framing changes, but it doesn't move
docs.motionClassicWhat: It crops into the image, scales that piece back up to the original size, and shifts the speed slightly. Your video is a little tighter, and each copy is tighter in a different spot. The framing stays FIXED from start to finish.
docs.motionClassicExample: Concrete example: on a video where you're filmed full-body, the copy cuts a few centimetres off the top and one side. On Gentle nobody notices; on Strong the copy is clearly tighter on you, slightly tilted, and plays a little faster.
docs.motionClassicSpecs:
GENTLE — crop-zoom 1.10× to 1.18×, speed ±1 to 3% (audio follows, no drift), no tilt. Image area lost ≈ 17 to 28%.
STRONG — crop-zoom 1.22× to 1.36×, speed ±4 to 8%, plus a fixed tilt of ±0.6 to 1.5°. Image area lost ≈ 33 to 46%.
In both cases: crop position drawn at random, framing fixed from start to finish.
docs.motionClassicWhen: When to use it: Gentle by default, when you want to stay as close as possible to the original. Switch to Strong if your copies still get flagged — checking the crop doesn't cut something important (a caption at the bottom, a logo in a corner).
docs.motionDynamicTitle: Advanced motion — a choreography replayed differently on every copy
docs.motionDynamicWhat: It's the only one of the three where the framing isn't fixed. And it isn't one slow move from start to finish: the camera strings MOMENTS together. It eases in toward a point, then snaps back to normal framing, settles, slides right, does an instant zoom « pop », eases back… The order and the durations change on every copy.
docs.motionDynamicExample: Concrete example: the camera creeps toward your face for 2 seconds, then the image snaps back to normal framing. A second of calm, then it slides left, a « pop » jolts it forward, and it eases back into place. The next copy will play a completely different sequence.
docs.motionDynamicSpecs:
Four kinds of moment: progressive zoom toward a point • snap back to normal framing then a 0.4 to 1.2 s pause • progressive slide from edge to edge • zoom « pop » followed by a progressive return. A slow move and a rupture always alternate. Speed is never modified.

STRONG — progressive zoom 1.08× to 1.22×, pop 1.20× to 1.32× (instant), slide up to 30% of the width, moves of 1 to 2.4 s. Image area lost: 0% at rest, up to 43% at the peak of a pop.
GENTLE — progressive zoom 1.03× to 1.10×, pop 1.07× to 1.15×, slides half as long, moves of 1.6 to 3 s, and the return to normal framing takes 0.2 s instead of a hard cut. Image area lost: 0% at rest, ~18% at most.

On videos longer than ~20 s the choreography loops (an 18 to 26 s cycle, itself drawn at random). The cycle restarts from neutral framing, so the seam doesn't show.
docs.motionDynamicWhen: When to use it: it's the most effective of the three against content matching, because two copies never look alike at ANY moment. Take STRONG by default; switch to GENTLE if you care about your framing and don't want to crop the image. Shake has left this pack: it's an independent option you can tick alongside any pack.
docs.motionStackBody: Yes, but it isn't advised: the zooms MULTIPLY. Motion (Strong) plus Advanced motion gives about 1.66× of zoom — nearly two thirds of the area cropped away — and the speed changes add up. Pick ONE pack instead, and turn its toggle to Strong if the result isn't enough.

metadata.label: Metadata

metadata_technical.label: Technical metadata
metadata_technical.hint: video bitrate, GOP, fps, H.264 profile
metadata_technical.help: Video bitrate 3–22 Mb/s • GOP 30–500 • H.264 profile (baseline/main/high) • Random FPS.

pixel_magic.label: Magic pixel
pixel_magic.help: Adds imperceptible luma noise to every pixel, every frame. Changes the file hash with no visible change.

audio.label: Audio
audio.help: Volume ±2 dB • Small random EQ peak (100–8,000 Hz, +1.5 dB) • Audio bitrate 96–192 kb/s. Stays subtle.

motion.label: Motion
motion.help:
Crops into the image, scales it back up, and shifts the speed slightly. The framing stays FIXED from start to finish.
Two intensities, chosen on the card:
• Gentle — zoom 1.10× to 1.18×, speed ±1 to 3%. Subtle, ~17 to 28% of the area cropped.
• Strong — zoom 1.22× to 1.36×, speed ±4 to 8%, plus a slight fixed tilt. Two copies no longer overlap, but ~33 to 46% of the area is cropped.

motion_dynamic.label: Advanced motion
motion_dynamic.help:
The only pack where the image moves DURING playback — and not as one continuous move: a sequence of linked moments.
Progressive zoom toward a point (centre, left, right, a corner…) • Snap back to normal framing • Progressive slide from one side to the other • Zoom « pop », then a progressive return.
Two intensities, chosen on the card:
• Strong — the boldest setting, zooms up to 1.32×.
• Gentle — same choreography at half the amplitude (zooms up to 1.15×), slower moves and softened returns. To avoid cropping the image too much.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Concretely, what gets changed in my videos?
faq.a1: Three things, none visible: the file metadata (device, date, encoder, geolocation), the visual signature via micro-variations below the perception threshold, and a unique binary fingerprint (modified hash and container). The file is then fully re-encoded, not duplicated. Your edit, your audio, your captions and your framing stay strictly identical to the original.
faq.a2: No. The original resolution and bitrate are preserved: a 1080p source stays 1080p, a 4K stays 4K. The file is rebuilt without extra compression — no visible loss on screen.
faq.q3: How many variants can I generate from a single video?
faq.a3: Up to 20 variants per video. The number of videos per month depends on your plan: the free plan lets you generate your first variants without a card, the Solo and Pro plans unlock volume.
faq.q4: Does it work on TikTok, Instagram and YouTube?
faq.a4: Yes. DuupFlow prepares the files, you post them wherever you want: TikTok, Instagram, YouTube, and any other platform.
faq.a5: A few minutes. Count roughly 3 minutes for 20 video variants, depending on the length and resolution of your source.

detected.title: My videos get flagged as non-original
detected.intro: Duplicating a file isn't always enough: algorithms compare what the video LOOKS LIKE, not just the file and its metadata. When copies still get flagged as non-original, two causes come up almost every time.
detected.light: Settings that were too light — if the filters you applied stay subtle, the copy still looks like the original to the naked eye. To an algorithm, two near-identical images are simply identical: raise the intensity, turn on mirror (reverse), add a motion pack and a watermark.
detected.tooMany: Too many copies from the same video — rarer, but if one copy gets caught, the others made from the same source can go down with it. Space out your posts and limit how many copies you make per source video.
detected.reco: 💡 What actually works: instead of 10 copies with light settings, make 3 or 4 with bold ones (reverse + motion + watermark). The copy has to look visibly different, not just differ inside the file.

how.title: How the AI Editor works
how.intro: The AI Editor doesn't edit on its own in a corner: YOUR Claude does the editing, and DuupFlow gives it eyes (your reference) and hands (your material). Three one-time steps, then everything happens in conversation.
how.s1: Connect your Claude — copy the connector address, paste it into Claude (Settings → Connectors → Add custom connector), then click Authorise. Once and for all, and it works on claude.ai, Claude Desktop and mobile — even on the free plan.
how.s2: Add a reference — the video that performed. DuupFlow pulls out its hook, pacing, cuts and transcript.
how.s3: Add your material — your footage, images and sounds, with a short description for each.
how.s4: Talk to your Claude — ask it to reproduce the reference using your material. Variants show up live in your DuupFlow workspace.
how.reco: 💡 Worth remembering: the editing is driven from your Claude conversation, not from DuupFlow. DuupFlow is where you drop the files and collect the videos.

ref.title: Which video to use as a reference
ref.intro: The reference is the model to reproduce. Two ways to use it, exactly the same move.
ref.mine: Your own video — already edited. Then add the files you used to make it: you get variants of your video.
ref.competitor: A competitor's video — the AI analyses its STRUCTURE (hook, pacing, cuts, text style), never its content. With your material, you get your version of what works.
ref.input: File or link — MP4 and MOV by drag and drop, or paste a link. Public TikTok and YouTube work straight away; Instagram may require you to be signed in.
ref.reco: 💡 A short, sharp reference beats a long one: it's the structure that gets copied, not the length.

prompt.title: What to ask your Claude
prompt.intro: Claude edits from what you tell it. The « Copy the prompt » button in your workspace gives you a ready-made starting point — after that, it's an ordinary conversation.
prompt.look: Have it look first — ask it to analyse the reference and explain in three lines what makes it work, BEFORE it builds anything.
prompt.several: Ask for several versions — « make me 3, using a different clip for each shot ».
prompt.iterate: Correct as you go — « the hook is too long », « make the subtitles yellow », « cut on the music ». It rebuilds the variant.
prompt.describe: Describe your files — the short description under each file (« product shot, front view ») is what lets it put the right shot in the right place.
prompt.reco: 💡 No technical vocabulary needed: talk to it the way you'd talk to an editor.

novariant.title: My variants aren't showing up
novariant.intro: Variants are created from your Claude conversation and appear in your workspace on their own. When nothing arrives, it's almost always one of these four causes.
novariant.connector: The connector is no longer authorised — Claude says it can't reach DuupFlow: click « Reconnect Claude » and authorise again.
novariant.ref: The reference isn't analysed — until the badge reads « structure analysed », Claude has nothing to reproduce. Run the analysis again.
novariant.material: No material — with no files to edit, it can't build anything: it only ever uses YOUR material.
novariant.quota: Quota reached — every rendered variant counts as one video, in the same counter as duplication. Rendering is blocked outright until quota frees up.
novariant.reco: ⏳ Variants are temporary: download the ones you want to keep. Your reference and your material stay put.

limits.title: What the AI Editor won't do
limits.intro: Three deliberate limits. Knowing them saves you from asking the same thing ten different ways.
limits.material: No footage that didn't come from you — no stock library, no generated b-roll, no outside assets. No suitable file in your material means no such shot.
limits.editorial: No editorial calls on your behalf — it cuts silences, hesitations and repeats. Reordering your point, summarising it or picking « the best bit »: no, that stays your job.
limits.motion: Heavy motion design is approximated — 3D, particles, morphs: it reproduces the intent (layout, pacing, colours, text), not the effect pixel for pixel.
limits.reco: 💡 The bar is the structure: same moments, same pacing, same text style. Not a frame-by-frame copy.
